proof_scope: In progress. R1772 constructs an actual compactly supported smooth cutoff rho, equal to one on [-1,1], zero outside [-2,2], and bounded in norm by one. Its dyadic differences chi_j=rho(xi/2^(j+1))-rho(xi/2^j) are actual compactly supported Schwartz functions, vanish at and outside the prescribed annular boundaries, and satisfy an exact finite telescoping identity. Closed dyadic annuli have overlap at most three, including boundary points needed for derivative supports. Exact dilation identities give uniform pointwise square-sum bounds for every derivative order of chi_j and q_j=i*2*pi*xi*chi_j with weights 2^(-2j). The five R1771 coefficient hypotheses are fully discharged. For the actual bands, total unweighted L2 energy and weighted transported derivative energy are uniformly bounded over every finite index set; an actual Fourier-tail bound with individual thresholds follows. L2 convergence of the telescoping band sums and band isolation remain.

Its norm bound uses the real bump's range [0,1]; its distance from f is controlled by the R=2 grid low-frequency estimate.
